title: Spark separates its Prime Foundation from a distinct Spark Assets Foundation for real-world asset deployment
content:
Two separate legal entities appear in Spark's Agent Creation parameters. A.6.1.1.1.2.1.1.3.1.1.4 names the **Spark Foundation** as "the Prime Foundation associated with Spark," with a mandate "to support the development, growth, and adoption of Spark." A.6.1.1.1.2.1.1.3.1.1.6.1 then adds the **Spark Assets Foundation**, an entity whose purpose is "to support the Spark Liquidity Layer through real world engagements and allocations," which "will deploy assets which are held in the ALM Contracts."

The split follows the boundary between on-chain and off-chain activity. Development, growth and adoption can be pursued entirely through code and governance. Real-world allocations require an entity that can sign contracts with counterparties, hold legal title, and be sued — a very different risk and compliance surface.

Putting that surface in a separate foundation means legal exposure from real-world engagements does not sit on the entity that stewards Spark's core development. It also creates a distinct control question: assets held in the ALM Contracts are deployed by an entity outside the protocol, so the guarantees on those assets are contractual and jurisdictional rather than purely programmatic.

This is registered as a *custom* Instance Parameter of the Agent Creation Primitive — the standard Agent template supplies one Prime Foundation, and Spark's real-world ambitions required extending it.
description: The Prime Foundation's mandate is development, growth and adoption; a second entity exists solely to make real-world engagements and deploy assets held in the ALM Contracts.
